title: Finite-free scalar extension of the intrinsic semilinear proper/open mate
statement:
Let $A_1\leftarrow A_2\leftarrow\cdots$ and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be inverse sequences of commutative rings with a compatible unital map $A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$. Assume there are a finite integer $d\geq1$ and compatible $A_n$-bases of $B_n$ of rank $d$: every transition carries each basis vector to the corresponding basis vector. On fixed small pro-etale sites of schemes $T$, use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\mathscr S_{C,T})$ of strict semilinear $(C_n)_T$-module systems, $C=A,B$, and derived scalar extension $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_\bullet}B_\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A strict system consists of module sheaves $M_n$ with linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$, and componentwise morphisms commuting with transitions.

Let $k:U\hookrightarrow V$, $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$ be quasi-compact open immersions and $r:U\to W$, $p:V\to Z$ proper morphisms with $pk=ir$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. No absolute separatedness or Cartesian hypothesis is imposed. Write $P_{v,C}\dashv S_{v,C}$ for exact inverse image and total derived direct image, and $J_{a,C}\dashv P_{a,C}$ for exact extension by zero. Let $\Gamma_{Q,C}:J_{i,C}S_{r,C}\to S_{p,C}J_{k,C}$ be the intrinsic proper/open mate of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting], normalized by its open unit and clopen component projection. For every $v$ define $\chi_v:T S_{v,A}\to S_{v,B}T$ as the $P_{v,B}\dashv S_{v,B}$ transpose of $T(\varepsilon_{v,A})$ after $P_{v,B}T\cong TP_{v,A}$. Let $\beta_a:TJ_{a,A}\cong J_{a,B}T$ be canonical open tensor balancing, the open projection isomorphism with second factor $B_\bullet$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Then, for every $M\in D(\mathscr S_{A,U})$,
$$S_{p,B}(\beta_{k,M})\circ\chi_{p,J_{k,A}M}\circ T_Z(\Gamma_{Q,A,M})
=\Gamma_{Q,B,T_UM}\circ J_{i,B}(\chi_{r,M})\circ\beta_{i,S_{r,A}M}.$$
This is an equality in $D(\mathscr S_{B,Z})$ before evaluation or total inverse limit, retaining all quotient transitions. The scalar direct-image comparisons obey composition with the canonical direct-image compositors, so this square may be whiskered by an outer proper direct image. The maps commute with the canonical cochain shifts. No constructibility, normalization, finite-Tor or boundedness hypothesis on $M$ is required.

proof.text: Publicly reexport the unchanged scalar construction data and its existing exactness and invertibility proofs. No new data are chosen.

Instantiate exchangeMate_cube with the A/B inverse-image adjunctions for r and p, the four scalar functors, inverse ell_r and ell_p and the open balancing beta_i and beta_k. The cube hypothesis is scalarIntrinsicAlphaCube. By the definitions of chi and gamma, its conclusion is the first conjunct verbatim.

Apply scalarInverseImageCoherence. Whisker ell_(v≫w) by pComp_A and the composite ell_w/ell_v square by pComp_B; their equality is exactly the first coherence clause. Apply mateEquiv to this equality and use conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp, mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp and mateEquiv_hcomp. Evaluating yields the displayed chi composition equation because sComp is the conjugate of pComp. Repeat with the vertical identity square and pId, then cancel the sId_B inverse to obtain the identity equation.

Exact-derived natural isomorphisms and composition isomorphisms commute with shifts, so ell does. The direct adjunction shift of diagramOpenClopenShiftModels and the generic shifted mate lemma yield the chi shift. For betaInv unfold the inverse mate word and use shift compatibility of the two open adjunctions and ell inverse; taking the inverse iso gives beta. For gamma, the geometric squareP is a composite of exact-derived comparison maps. Its inverse open mate betaInv and beta therefore commute with shifts. The proved diagram model helpers give the shifts of pi, pComp and jComp; equality transports commute by eliminating the equality. Substitution into alpha proves its shift compatibility, then the generic mate-shift lemma gives gamma for A and B.
